text:
alex: Heads-up — saw tail-latency spike in prod-eu during a 1m QPS burst. Pods stuck Pending, CA didn't scale nodes fast enough :eyes:

maria: logs? pending reason?

alex: kubectl get pods | grep Pending
```
mymodel-7f8c9d6b-xyz   0/5 nodes available: 5 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
``` 

kevin: warm-pool size is 2 for eu-gpu-pool but those nodes have taint reserved=preemptible:NoSchedule. Scheduler won't place non-tolerated pods. CA sees pending pods and starts to create on-demand nodes -> cost spike + latency

tara: HPA was triggered by external metric 'requests_per_second' from prometheus-adapter with 30s scrape, no debounce. It spun up ~40 pods quickly.
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: requests_per_second
      target:
        type: Value
        value: "100"
```

alex: seems like three signals raced: noisy external metric -> HPA rapid pod creation -> CA adds nodes -> scheduler can't use warm nodes because of taints/tolerations mismatch. Also adapter returns short spikes from client retries.

kevin: short-term fixes:
- set HPA.behavior.scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 60
- add left-smoothing in prometheus-adapter query (avg_over_time(..., 1m))
- create small 'gpu-burst' nodepool without the preemptible taint (min 1, max 3)

autoscale-bot: [1723456900] cluster-autoscaler: scaled up nodegroup eu-gpu-pool by 3 nodes (reason: 38 unschedulable pods)

maria: agreed. add monitoring alert for 'pending_pods > 10 for 2m' and cost alert for 'gpu.on_demand_spend > $2000/day'

tara: cost tradeoff: gpu-burst pool (~3 on-demand gpus) adds ~ $7k/mo but prevents 1-2hrs of app tail latency per month. Canarize the change for 24h on EU region.

kevin: i'll open a PR: HPA config + prometheus-adapter smoothing + terraform for gpu-burst pool + CA expander policy to prefer existing nodegroups. assigning @maria for canary watch.

alex: putting a snippet of prom query we used:
```
avg_over_time(sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="frontend"}[30s]))[1m])
```

maria: thx. pinging @kevin once PR is up. :thumbsup:
